notable_absence.finding: Unlike advancedGetOp.md and every other CAS/error-showing page in this batch, this page's configuration comment omits the 6.6.x/7.0(non-.2) legacy tiers entirely and cites only 'Version 7.0.2+' - consistent with the Capella twin's own observation of the same variation.

cross_component_finding: This page's failure-path log for the missing-key GET shows `"code": 1` (`{"error": {"code": 1, "name": "LCB_KEY_ENOENT", "desc": "The document key does not exist on the server", "key_not_found": true}, "success": false}`), whereas the sibling advancedGetOp.md's failure log for the byte-identical error name and desc text ('The document key does not exist on the server') shows `"code": 272` - the same identical error (LCB_KEY_ENOENT / ENOENT / key_not_found:true) is documented under two different numeric codes on two sibling pages in the same handler family. This looks like a docs inconsistency (a stale or mistyped code) rather than a real semantic difference between the cached and uncached GET paths, and is worth a docs-issue.
